=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:`_trend_single_table`, page loop: `more = len(page_runs) >= TREND_PER_PAGE or (total is not None and total > read)` followed by `if page >= max_pages or len(page_runs) < TREND_PER_PAGE: table["reason"] = "history_truncated"` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A full page counts as "more pages exist" even when `total_count` shows every run was read. The query filters on `created=>=<window_start>`, so `covers_window` is practically never true.
  WHY: With total_count=200, the table gets `history=truncated` and regression is never computed, so it reports `regression=false ... history=truncated` with outcome `partial`. With total_count=100, an extra empty page-2 GET is made. Suggested fix: `more = (total > read) if total is not None else len(page_runs) >= TREND_PER_PAGE`.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:`_heal_build_run_time_trend`, the summaries loop that sets `trend_conclusion="timed_out"` when `jq -e '... | any(. == "timed_out")'` matches any `${LOG_DIR}/run-${trend_run_id}-jobs.json`. This feeds `classify_failure_shape` (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py lines 4011-4013) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The conclusion passed to the classifier is an OR across all reported runs (up to MAX_RUNS=3 run_refs, line 321, loop at line 1759), while the classifier docstring describes the input as "the failed job's conclusion".
  WHY: A current test failure with an earlier timed-out run_ref is classified `timeout` and gets the trend section plus up to 6 GETs. The reviewer downgraded this from MAJOR because SIGNATURE (line 1905) and FAILING_TESTS_JSON (line 2579) are aggregated across runs the same way and the effect never blocks filing. Narrower option: take the conclusion from the first run_ref only.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:`classify_failure_shape` docstring, lines 4002-4003: "Nothing calls it yet (P3 step 1 / D3); later phases wire it into the heal intake." | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The PR adds the first caller (`run_time_trend`), and `test_classify_failure_shape_has_no_caller_yet` now asserts exactly one caller, which contradicts both its own name and the docstring.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime, but maintainers may treat a change to the function's precedence as safe when it now gates the trend API calls.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  PROBLEM: `trend_conclusion` is set to `timed_out` if any job in any summarized run timed out, instead of using only the current run's conclusion.
  WHY: `classify_failure_shape` is then forced to a `timeout` shape, so non-stall and non-timeout failures get a `## Run-time trend` section and extra API calls.

  WHY: When the run count is an exact multiple of 100, an empty page-2 request is made. When 200 runs are read, `page >= max_pages` sets `history=truncated` and suppresses `regression=true`.

  PROBLEM: The docstring still says "Nothing calls it yet (P3 step 1 / D3)...", but `run_time_trend` now calls the function.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:lines 6502, 6506-6508, inside `_trend_single_table` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The truncation branch fires on `page >= max_pages` whether or not more pages exist. With total_count=200 read in two pages, `more` stays True and `reason=history_truncated` is set. The spec scopes truncation to the case where "more pages exist", but the code never checks `total > read`.
  WHY: A complete read is marked `history=truncated` and `regression=false`, which masks the signal the feature is meant to expose. Suggested fix: gate truncation on `total is None or total > read`.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 3190-3203 in `_heal_build_run_time_trend`, combined with `classify_failure_shape` ordering at scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:4011-4013 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `trend_conclusion` becomes `"timed_out"` if any run in `SUMMARIES_FILE` (the failure streak) timed out. The classifier checks timeout before failing tests, so the current test_failure run is misclassified as `"timeout"`.
  WHY: A current test failure, crash or api_error in a streak whose earlier run timed out gets a trend section and 6 API calls, contrary to the spec. No test covers this case. Suggested fix: inspect only the `PHASE_FAILED_RUN_ID` run (see line 1775).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:line 3227: `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1 python3 "${HEAL_PY}" run-time-trend --repo "${SOURCE_REPO}" \` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The variable has no effect because `_last_green_run_gh` (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:6096-6097) calls `subprocess.run` directly.
  WHY: Nothing fails today, but the setting is misleading and could silently break retries if the runner is swapped.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:lines 4002-4003 (docstring of `classify_failure_shape`) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: "Nothing calls it yet" is stale now that `run_time_trend` calls the function (line 6686), and tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:10838 asserts exactly one caller.
  WHY: Nothing fails today, but the stale docstring risks an accidental API break in a future PR.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:line 10838: `def test_classify_failure_shape_has_no_caller_yet() -> None:` | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The name says "has_no_caller_yet", but the inverted body now asserts exactly one caller (line 10856).
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime, but the test name is misleading.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
